Museum of Pre-Columbian Art

Clay, wood and metal seen as art

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

The museum presents pre-Columbian works as art, with opportunities to compare form across clay, wood and metal. The most rewarding stop is often a single case where the lighting brings the silhouette or surface into clear relief.

Planning your visit

60–90 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Clay, wood and metal seen as art

Study a vessel against the background of its case, then look along its rim. That change of angle helps distinguish painted lines from contours formed by the potter's hand.

Getting there

Get directions

History and local experience

Look for a motif repeated in objects of two materials. In metal it may be defined by reflected light; in clay a painted outline or a modelled edge may carry the same idea.

Walking route

  1. Plazoleta Nazarenas, Museo de Arte Precolombino, Cusco
  2. Enter from Plazoleta Nazarenas, note the gallery sequence around the house and choose two objects of different materials to compare.
  3. Return to the plaza for an exterior view of the entrance.
